title: Deployment Guardian: policy synthesis for multi-tier fallbacks and cross-region rollbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a ‘Deployment Guardian’ policy synthesizer that produces deterministic fallback and rollback plans for model variant deployments across regions and capacity tiers. The guardian will evaluate compatibility probes, live KPIs (latency, error, quality regressions), and tiered capacity availability to decide: immediate failover to a compatible variant, capacity-tier downgrade, regional routing, or automated rollback. The goal is to reduce MTTR for bad canaries while preserving capacity guarantees for high-tier customers and avoiding noisy rollbacks for transient infra noise.

Why this work:
- Current fallbacks are ad-hoc per-deployment and often either too aggressive (unnecessary rollbacks) or too slow (long outages).
- We need a canonical policy that codifies: compatibility scoring, graded fallbacks (variant -> quantized variant -> cached response -> regional failover), and SLO-aware thresholds for automated actions.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: policy synthesis engine, probes API, compatibility scoring hooks, integration with routing layer and rollout controller, dashboards and alerting.
- Non-goals: model retraining, on-the-fly kernel selection changes, upstream billing changes.

Design overview:
1) Compatibility probe pass: lightweight test requests run during canary traffic and periodically on live variants. Probes exercise tokenization, prompt hooks, and KV cache behavior. Probe results feed a compatibility score (0-100).
2) KPI windows and anomaly detector: streaming metrics (95th latency, p50 latency, error rate, quality regression score from eval probes) computed in 15s and 5m windows with anomaly scoring.
3) Tier-aware fallback graph: compile a prioritized graph of fallback targets per request class:
   - Primary: same-variant in same-region
   - Secondary: compatible-variant (quantized or distilled) in same-region
   - Tertiary: fallback to cached prefix response or downstream cached embeddings
   - Quaternary: cross-region compatible-variant in preferred failover region
   - Last-resort: routing to degraded-cost tier with strict rate limiting
4) Action synthesizer: given compatibility score, KPI anomalies, and available capacity reservations, synthesize an ordered set of actions with confidence and rollback thresholds. Actions have soft/automatic vs hard/manual labels.
5) Safety gates: policy must respect reserved capacity for Dedicated customers; automated downgrade cannot exceed configured percent of reserved throughput without explicit approval.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: compatibility probe service + probe spec and SDK hooks (ENG + Research pairing).
- Week 2: streaming KPI windows + simple anomaly detector using z-score heuristics; build metric mapping to action triggers.
- Week 3: policy graph compiler, fallback candidate catalog, and simple action synthesizer prototype.
- Week 4: integrate with rollout controller, add safety gates for reserved capacity, build canary playbook and test harness.
- Week 5: end-to-end test cases, chaos scenarios, and canary traffic rehearsals; dashboards and alerting setup.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- Automated rollback triggers on quality regressions >= 15% measured by eval probe in 5m window and sustained for 2 windows.
- Latency anomaly (p95 > baseline * 2.5) sustained for 3 consecutive 15s windows triggers a tiered fallback action (not immediate full rollback).
- Policy respects reserved capacity: no automated downgrade that reduces reserved throughput by >10% without manual approval.
- Integration tests that simulate cross-region failover complete within defined SLA targets and exercises the fallback graph.
- Postmortem drill: roll a bad canary in staging and verify the Deployment Guardian executes the expected action set.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New dashboards: Deployment Guardian decisions log, compatibility score distribution, action execution latency, count of automated rollbacks by reason.
- Alerts: guardian-decision-failure, auto-rollback-suppressed-due-to-reservation, repeated-fallback-flap (>3 actions in 5m).

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (internal): run guardian in passive mode (decisions logged, no actions) on internal staging clusters for 2 weeks.
- Stage 2 (canary): enable soft automated actions for low-tier test deployments only. Observe for 1 week.
- Stage 3 (gradual): enable auto actions for non-reserved production customers with 24/7 guardrail monitoring.
- Stage 4 (full): opt-in for Dedicated customers; require customer opt-in to allow auto-downgrade of reserved capacity.

Operational playbook highlights:
- Manual override endpoints for immediate freeze of guardian actions per-org or globally.
- Post-action checklist: link to rollout PR, canary traffic snapshot, compatibility probe report.
- Escalation: if repeated flapping detected, the guardian will escalate to oncall and open a roll-forward remediation ticket.

Security and compliance notes:
- Probes must not leak customer data; use synthetic prompt templates or redacted inputs.
- Audit logs for every synthesized action must include decision inputs (compatibility score, metric snapshots) and be retained per company retention policy.

Next steps and deliverables:
- PR for probe service and probe spec: GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1187
- Design doc: drive.redwood.ai/docs/deployment-guardian-design-v1 (link internal)
- Test harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/guardian-tests (seeded with scenario matrix)

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- Conservative rollbacks reduce false positives but increase MTTR; we prefer prioritized graded fallbacks to balance availability and quality.
- Cross-region failover increases latency and costs; policy must include SLO-aware gating that prefers degraded local fallbacks first.
- Complexity vs observability: policy graphs should be auditable and exportable to human-readable YAML for troubleshooting.
